text:
maria gonzalez: Quick sync — ran a short runbook exploring a "precision ladder" for cost-sensitive endpoints. Trying fp8 -> int8 -> 4bit fallback with a safety net, and I have some surprising noise on mid-length prompts (~40-90 tokens).

dmitri kovalenko: can you summarize the ladder and the safety net? are we switching weights only or accumulators too?

maria gonzalez: initial prototype: weights quantized to target precision, accumulators stay fp16 except for final matmul which we downcast. safety: if per-token logprob delta > 0.25 vs shadow baseline for 5 tokens, rollback to previous rung.

rachel: interesting. did you test per-layer 4-bit for feedforward only vs attention-only? often ffns are less sensitive.

maria gonzalez: yes — ffns tolerated 4bit fairly well. attention downcast introduces more entropy. looks like attention QK scaling and softmax tails get noisy.

chen li: can you paste the quant-profile json you used? helps to reason about runtime knobs.

maria gonzalez: pasted below:
```json
{
  "profile_name": "ladder-alpha",
  "rungs": [
    {"name":"fp8-attn-int8-ffn","attn":"fp8","ffn":"int8","accum":"fp16"},
    {"name":"int8-all","attn":"int8","ffn":"int8","accum":"fp16"},
    {"name":"4bit-ffn-only","attn":"int8","ffn":"4bit","accum":"fp16"}
  ],
  "safety": {"rollback_logprob_delta": 0.25, "streak": 5}
}
```

dmitri kovalenko: thanks. two quick asks: 1) add a per-layer clamp threshold for softmax inputs to detect outlier logits, 2) capture qkv scale distributions.

maria gonzalez: added softmax clamp probe in next run. initial micro-bench shows ~8% token-level top1 mismatch at rung1 vs fp16 baseline after token 50. ramping.

rachel: ops question: how hard is it to expose rung selection as a per-customer routing rule in the control plane? want ability to opt-in for early customers.

chen li: trivial to add config flag in profile: "forced_rung": "int8-all". Making it dynamic via rollout is slightly more work but supported. more concerning: long-kv contexts amplify small softmax shifts — I suggest a length-based accumulator override: keep attn accumulators fp16 after length > 64.

dmitri kovalenko: agreed, length-based accumulator override seems like a low-risk knob. we should estimate cost: how many tokens per request are >64 in production?

maria gonzalez: ops telemetry: ~12% of requests exceed 64 tokens, ~3% exceed 256. so targeted accumulator upgrade would hit small fraction of traffic.

rachel: proposal: three mitigations
- add "length_accum_threshold" to quant profiles (default 128)
- add softmax-clamp probe + early-rollback rule (streak sensitive)
- add per-layer 4bit opt-in for FFN only

chen li: + implement a small regression suite: 100 sampled prompts, compare KL, top1 mismatch, and hallucination checklist. we should also produce a monotonicity test: ensure model quality does not oscillate as we step down ladder for the same prompt sequence.

maria gonzalez: i'll run that suite tomorrow and attach artifacts. also will include a tiny synthetic that reproduces the softmax-saturation pattern.

dmitri kovalenko: runtime-safety discussion: do we prefer rollback to previous rung or immediate full-fp16 fallback? rollback minimizes cost but might still degrade if previous rung was bad. full-fp16 is safest but expensive. Ops input?

rachel: for new customers choose rollback-first, and for sensitive customers or SLA contracts do immediate fp16 fallback. that maps cleanly to Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.

ops-bot: Created INF-5201: "precision-ladder playbook + length-accum threshold prototype" assigned to maria gonzalez, chen li.

chen li: small implementation note: when accumulating in fp16 but storing kv in quantized form we need a deterministic cast on replay to avoid seed-sensitive drift. add a tiny checksum on kv entries to detect silent corruption.

maria gonzalez: good call. will add a hashed-kv checksum probe.

dmitri kovalenko: final thought: could we compress the ladder into a single hybrid kernel that uses block-wise mixed precision (e.g., per-head 4bit if head variance low)? more invasive but might get us cost wins without whole-model switches. food for R&D.

rachel: yes, file as R&D spike. ops: let's plan small canary next week for "int8-all" rung on 5% traffic with rollback enabled. who owns rollout?

dmitri kovalenko: i'll coordinate with runtime and set up canary.

maria gonzalez: thanks all, i'll upload perf artifacts + reg-suite results to INF-5201 when done. :wave:
